claims.explanation: Docetaxel kills cells by stabilizing microtubules, and selectivity across these lines is best explained by the expression of its direct tubulin targets and by the integrity of the mitotic-spindle assembly checkpoint and apoptosis machinery rather than by any single lineage or driver mutation. Lines with high TUBB3/TUBB (class III/other beta-tubulin) and low drug-efflux or high apoptotic priming are most sensitive, while lines with low tubulin expression, high ABCB1 efflux, or defective spindle-checkpoint/apoptosis signaling survive. The pattern of sensitive lines (many TP53-mutant, PIK3CA/PTEN-altered carcinomas) is consistent with loss of G1/S checkpoints forcing reliance on mitotic arrest and apoptosis for drug-induced death.

features.basis: class III beta-tubulin is the direct docetaxel target; high expression increases microtubule binding and mitotic arrest
beta-tubulin is the primary docetaxel-binding subunit; expression level determines drug-target engagement
alpha-tubulin heterodimer partner required for docetaxel-stabilized microtubule polymer
P-glycoprotein efflux pump lowers intracellular docetaxel and is a canonical resistance mechanism
loss of p53-mediated G1/S arrest forces mitotic death after docetaxel-induced spindle damage; enriched in sensitive lines
anti-apoptotic BCL2 (an annotated docetaxel target) raises the apoptotic threshold and blunts mitotic catastrophe
tau (an annotated docetaxel target) competes with tubulin binding and modulates microtubule stability
MAP2 is an annotated docetaxel target that can sequester drug and alter microtubule dynamics
MAP4 is an annotated docetaxel target affecting microtubule stability and drug sensitivity
activating EGFR mutations drive proliferative/survival signaling and are enriched in the least-affected NSCLC lines
PXR (NR1I2) is an annotated docetaxel target that transcriptionally upregulates CYP3A4/ABCB1 detoxification
PTEN loss hyperactivates PI3K/AKT survival signaling but also impairs DNA-damage repair, and is enriched in sensitive lines
